[curious, lively, starts speaking immediately] That crossed-out price is a trick. It is called anchoring, and it works on almost everyone. Even when we know it. In nineteen seventy-four, psychologists spun a rigged wheel of fortune that could only ever stop on ten or sixty-five. Then they asked people a completely unrelated question. Those who saw sixty-five gave much bigger answers than those who saw ten. That first number becomes an anchor for everything. Your brain adjusts away from it, but almost never far enough. So a crossed-out two hundred makes ninety-nine feel like a steal. Ask yourself what you would pay without it.
